nodes.title: What linear algebra is actually studying
outcomes: Recognize vectors, linear combinations, and linear transformations as the recurring objects of the subject.
Switch between geometric, algebraic, and data views of the same simple vector problem.

nodes.title: Scalars, coordinates, tuples, and notation
outcomes: Read vector and matrix notation without treating symbols as unexplained decoration.
Distinguish a scalar from an ordered list of coordinates.

nodes.title: Vectors as displacement, data, and state
outcomes: Interpret the same vector as geometry, data, or system state depending on context.

nodes.title: Vector addition and scalar multiplication
outcomes: Compute and explain the two operations that define linear combination.

nodes.title: Linear combinations and weighted mixtures
outcomes: Build new vectors from weighted combinations and predict their geometric/data meaning.

nodes.title: Span: what combinations can reach
outcomes: Decide whether a target vector is reachable from given generators in simple cases.

nodes.title: Linear equations as constraints
outcomes: Interpret a linear equation geometrically and algebraically.

nodes.title: Systems of linear equations and solution sets
outcomes: Represent several simultaneous linear constraints and reason about zero, one, or many solutions.

nodes.title: Matrices as organized coefficients and operators
outcomes: Read rows, columns, entries, and dimensions and distinguish matrix-as-data from matrix-as-map.

nodes.title: Matrix-vector multiplication as a column combination
outcomes: Explain Ax as a linear combination of the columns of A rather than a memorized multiplication recipe.

nodes.title: Elimination: changing equations without changing solutions
outcomes: Use elementary row operations while preserving the solution set.

nodes.title: Pivots, free variables, and the geometry of solutions
outcomes: Connect pivots and free variables to uniqueness and families of solutions.

nodes.title: Linear transformations in the plane
outcomes: Recognize scaling, reflection, projection, rotation, and shear as transformations and test linearity informally.

nodes.title: Composition and matrix multiplication
outcomes: Explain matrix multiplication as composition of linear transformations.

nodes.title: Invertibility as reversible linear action
outcomes: Relate invertibility to unique solvability and reversible transformations.

nodes.title: L0 synthesis: solve, transform, and explain one problem three ways
outcomes: Integrate equation, vector, and transformation viewpoints in one worked task.

nodes.title: Vector spaces: the abstraction behind vectors
outcomes: State the vector-space axioms and recognize common finite-dimensional examples.

nodes.title: Subspaces and closure
outcomes: Test whether a subset is a subspace and explain closure.

nodes.title: Linear independence
outcomes: Determine whether generators contain redundancy and connect dependence to nontrivial combinations yielding zero.

nodes.title: Bases: minimal coordinates for a space
outcomes: Explain why a basis both spans and is independent.

nodes.title: Coordinates relative to a basis
outcomes: Convert vectors between abstract form and basis coordinates.

nodes.title: Dimension
outcomes: Explain dimension as basis size and use it as an invariant.

nodes.title: Column space
outcomes: Interpret the column space as all outputs Ax.

nodes.title: Null space
outcomes: Interpret the null space as inputs erased by a matrix.

nodes.title: Row space
outcomes: Relate row space to constraints and elimination.

nodes.title: Rank and rank-nullity
outcomes: Compute rank conceptually and use rank-nullity to connect inputs, outputs, and information loss.

nodes.title: Linear maps
outcomes: Define linearity precisely and reason about maps independently of coordinates.

nodes.title: Kernel and image
outcomes: Generalize null space and column space to arbitrary linear maps.

nodes.title: Matrix representation of a linear map
outcomes: Construct a matrix representation once domain and codomain bases are chosen.

nodes.title: Change of basis and similarity
outcomes: Explain why one linear map can have different matrices in different bases.

nodes.title: Isomorphisms and structural sameness
outcomes: Recognize when two finite-dimensional vector spaces are structurally equivalent.

nodes.title: Determinants as signed volume scaling
outcomes: Interpret determinant geometrically before using formulas.

nodes.title: Determinant properties and computation
outcomes: Use multiplicativity, row operations, and triangular structure to reason about determinants.

nodes.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
outcomes: Identify directions preserved by a linear transformation up to scaling.

nodes.title: Characteristic polynomial
outcomes: Connect eigenvalues to roots of det(A-λI).

nodes.title: Diagonalization
outcomes: Explain when an eigenbasis turns a map into independent scalar actions.

nodes.title: Inner products, length, and angle
outcomes: Define inner products and recover norms, angles, and orthogonality.

nodes.title: Orthogonality and orthogonal complements
outcomes: Reason about perpendicular subspaces and decompositions.

nodes.title: Orthogonal projection
outcomes: Derive projection onto a line/subspace and connect it to closest-point approximation.

nodes.title: Gram-Schmidt and QR factorization
outcomes: Build an orthonormal basis and connect the process to QR.

nodes.title: Least squares
outcomes: Solve inconsistent systems by projection and interpret residual orthogonality.

nodes.title: L1 synthesis: the four-subspace and least-squares picture
outcomes: Integrate rank, nullity, orthogonality, and least squares in one structural model.

nodes.title: Complex vector spaces
outcomes: Extend finite-dimensional linear algebra from real to complex scalars.

nodes.title: Linear functionals and dual spaces
outcomes: Treat linear measurements as vectors in the dual space.

nodes.title: Transpose, adjoint, and annihilators
outcomes: Relate adjoints to inner products and annihilators to dual constraints.

nodes.title: Invariant subspaces
outcomes: Recognize subspaces preserved by an operator.

nodes.title: Triangularization
outcomes: Explain why invariant flags can expose operator structure.

nodes.title: Minimal polynomials
outcomes: Use annihilating polynomials to characterize operator structure.

nodes.title: Generalized eigenvectors and Jordan form
outcomes: Explain what diagonalization failure looks like and how Jordan chains repair the basis.

nodes.title: Normal, self-adjoint, unitary, and orthogonal operators
outcomes: Classify important operator families by adjoint relations.

nodes.title: Spectral theorem for real symmetric operators
outcomes: State and use orthogonal diagonalization for real symmetric matrices.

nodes.title: Spectral theorem for complex normal operators
outcomes: State and use unitary diagonalization for complex normal operators.

nodes.title: Positive definite and semidefinite matrices
outcomes: Connect positivity, eigenvalues, quadratic energy, and geometry.

nodes.title: Quadratic forms
outcomes: Classify and transform quadratic forms using symmetric matrices.

nodes.title: Singular values
outcomes: Interpret singular values as principal input-output stretch factors.

nodes.title: Singular value decomposition
outcomes: Factor a linear map into orthogonal directions and nonnegative stretches.

nodes.title: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse
outcomes: Use the pseudoinverse for least-squares and minimum-norm solutions.

nodes.title: Low-rank approximation and Eckart-Young
outcomes: Explain why truncated SVD is optimal for standard low-rank approximation norms.

nodes.title: Rank factorizations
outcomes: Construct compact factorizations exposing row/column space structure.

nodes.title: Direct sums and block matrices
outcomes: Decompose spaces and operators into interacting blocks.

nodes.title: Affine spaces and hyperplanes
outcomes: Separate linear subspaces from translated affine sets and interpret hyperplanes via functionals.

nodes.title: Bilinear and sesquilinear forms
outcomes: Generalize dot products and reason about form matrices.

nodes.title: Generalized inner products and metric matrices
outcomes: Work with weighted inner products and understand metric dependence.

nodes.title: Tensor products: building multilinear state spaces
outcomes: Understand the universal idea and basic coordinate construction of tensor products.

nodes.title: Exterior algebra and determinant structure
outcomes: Connect oriented volume and determinants to alternating multilinear structure.

nodes.title: Quotient spaces
outcomes: Model vectors modulo a subspace and connect quotient dimension to structure.

nodes.title: Canonical forms and classification viewpoint
outcomes: Recognize canonical forms as tools for classifying linear operators up to change of basis.

nodes.title: L2 proof studio: prove a structural theorem two ways
outcomes: Compare coordinate and coordinate-free proof strategies.

nodes.title: Floating-point arithmetic as a model, not real numbers
outcomes: Explain rounding, finite precision, and why exact algebraic identities can fail numerically.

nodes.title: Vector and matrix norms for error measurement
outcomes: Choose norms to measure vectors, operators, residuals, and perturbations.

nodes.title: Condition numbers: sensitivity of problems
outcomes: Separate problem sensitivity from algorithm quality.

nodes.title: Forward error, backward error, and stability
outcomes: Distinguish the error in an answer from the perturbation needed to explain it.

nodes.title: Gaussian elimination with pivoting
outcomes: Explain why pivoting changes numerical reliability even when exact algebra is unchanged.

nodes.title: LU factorization
outcomes: Derive LU from elimination and use it for repeated solves.

nodes.title: Cholesky factorization
outcomes: Exploit positive definiteness for efficient symmetric solves.

nodes.title: Householder reflections and Givens rotations
outcomes: Construct stable orthogonal transformations used by numerical factorizations.

nodes.title: QR algorithms for least squares
outcomes: Solve least squares without forming normal equations unnecessarily.

nodes.title: Computing the SVD
outcomes: Understand the numerical pipeline behind singular-value computation at a conceptual level.

nodes.title: Symmetric eigenvalue computation
outcomes: Connect reduction and iterative methods to stable symmetric eigenvalue algorithms.

nodes.title: Schur form and the nonsymmetric eigenproblem
outcomes: Use Schur form as a numerically stable replacement for fragile eigenvector bases.

nodes.title: Power and inverse iteration
outcomes: Analyze simple iterative eigenvalue methods and convergence.

nodes.title: QR iteration
outcomes: Explain how repeated QR factorizations reveal eigenvalues.

nodes.title: Krylov subspaces
outcomes: Build approximation spaces from repeated matrix action.

nodes.title: Arnoldi and Lanczos methods
outcomes: Approximate large eigenproblems using orthogonal Krylov bases.

nodes.title: Iterative methods for linear systems
outcomes: Contrast stationary/direct and Krylov iterative solving strategies.

nodes.title: Conjugate gradients
outcomes: Explain why SPD structure enables efficient Krylov minimization.

nodes.title: GMRES
outcomes: Understand residual minimization for general nonsymmetric systems.

nodes.title: Preconditioning
outcomes: Change a problem representation to accelerate iterative convergence without changing the desired solution.

nodes.title: Sparse matrices and storage
outcomes: Reason about sparsity structure, storage, and algorithmic consequences.

nodes.title: Structured matrices
outcomes: Recognize Toeplitz, banded, block, and other structure that algorithms can exploit.

nodes.title: Matrix functions and the exponential
outcomes: Define functions of matrices and connect exp(A) to dynamics.

nodes.title: Generalized eigenvalue problems
outcomes: Recognize and formulate problems of the form Ax=λBx.

nodes.title: PCA through covariance eigenvectors and SVD
outcomes: Derive PCA as a low-rank/spectral method rather than a black-box statistics recipe.

nodes.title: Graph Laplacians and spectral graph methods
outcomes: Translate graph structure into matrices and interpret low-frequency eigenvectors.

nodes.title: Markov chains and PageRank-style eigenvectors
outcomes: Connect stochastic evolution to invariant eigenvectors.

nodes.title: L3 numerical laboratory: accuracy, residual, and runtime
outcomes: Design a reproducible experiment comparing mathematically equivalent but numerically different methods.

nodes.title: Matrix perturbation theory
outcomes: Quantify how solutions and spectral objects move under perturbation.

nodes.title: Subspace perturbation and eigenvector sensitivity
outcomes: Reason about eigenspace sensitivity beyond scalar eigenvalue movement.

nodes.title: Pseudospectra and nonnormal matrices
outcomes: Explain transient behavior and spectral sensitivity that eigenvalues alone can hide.

nodes.title: Matrix inequalities and singular-value majorization
outcomes: Use advanced inequalities to compare spectra, singular values, and norms.

nodes.title: The positive semidefinite cone
outcomes: Treat PSD matrices geometrically and connect them to convex optimization.

nodes.title: Kronecker products and vectorization
outcomes: Manipulate separable matrix structure and vectorized operator identities.

nodes.title: Tensor decompositions
outcomes: Compare CP, Tucker, and matrix-SVD analogies while respecting higher-order differences.

nodes.title: Random projections and sketching
outcomes: Use random embeddings to reduce dimension while controlling geometric distortion.

nodes.title: Randomized low-rank approximation
outcomes: Construct randomized range finders and reason about pass complexity and error.

nodes.title: CUR and interpolative decompositions
outcomes: Approximate matrices using representative rows/columns and compare interpretability with SVD.

nodes.title: Streaming and out-of-core linear algebra
outcomes: Design algorithms when data cannot reside entirely in fast memory.

nodes.title: Mixed precision and iterative refinement
outcomes: Reason about using multiple precisions while recovering high-accuracy solutions.

nodes.title: Communication-avoiding and parallel linear algebra
outcomes: Treat data movement as a first-class cost in modern matrix algorithms.

nodes.title: Matrix-free methods
outcomes: Solve large problems using operator actions without explicitly forming A.

nodes.title: Differentiating through linear algebra operations
outcomes: Understand derivatives of solves, factorizations, and spectral operations and their failure modes.

nodes.title: Linear algebra inside large-scale optimization
outcomes: Identify the repeated linear-algebra kernels that dominate optimization algorithms.

nodes.title: High-dimensional geometry and random embeddings
outcomes: Connect concentration and random projections to scalable geometric reasoning.

nodes.title: L4 specialist project: choose a matrix problem and defend the algorithm
outcomes: Select methods from structure, accuracy, memory, and compute constraints and justify the choice.

nodes.title: Read a proof-heavy linear algebra paper
outcomes: Reconstruct definitions, theorem dependencies, proof strategy, and hidden assumptions from a research paper.

nodes.title: Read a numerical linear algebra paper
outcomes: Separate mathematical guarantee, implementation choice, benchmark design, and empirical claim.

nodes.title: Reproduce a matrix-factorization benchmark
outcomes: Reproduce a published numerical result with controlled environment and metrics.

nodes.title: Design a conditioning and stability experiment
outcomes: Construct adversarial and representative inputs that distinguish conditioning from instability.

nodes.title: Inspect BLAS/LAPACK-level implementation boundaries
outcomes: Map high-level factorizations to library kernels, layouts, and performance constraints.

nodes.title: Reproducible numerical methodology
outcomes: Report precision, hardware, software versions, seeds, residuals, tolerances, and failure criteria.

nodes.title: Research ethics for mathematical software and benchmarks
outcomes: Avoid cherry-picked matrices, hidden preprocessing, misleading speedups, and irreproducible claims.

nodes.title: Build a literature map and isolate an open linear algebra question
outcomes: Trace a research lineage and distinguish an open question from a vague topic.

nodes.title: Randomized numerical linear algebra frontier
outcomes: Compare current randomized/sketched methods and identify unresolved accuracy, communication, or robustness questions.

nodes.title: Tensor and multilinear algebra frontier
outcomes: Map active problems in identifiability, scalable decomposition, structured tensors, and applications.

nodes.title: Large-scale spectral and graph linear algebra frontier
outcomes: Identify open computational and theoretical issues in massive spectral problems.

nodes.title: Mixed-precision and hardware-aware linear algebra frontier
outcomes: Study current tradeoffs among precision, energy, communication, reliability, and accelerator architecture.

nodes.title: Trustworthy and reproducible numerical linear algebra frontier
outcomes: Formulate reliability questions spanning algorithms, software, benchmarks, and reproducibility.

nodes.title: Original linear algebra research project
outcomes: Formulate, execute, critique, and communicate a contribution-grade theoretical or computational investigation.
